O.outcome_detail: responsible interpretation of institutional analytics visualizations

cells.quote: Findings indicated that combining a structured framework with AI-based guidance can enhance context-aware, responsible interpretation of institutional data.
cells.note: The study used a qualitative think-aloud design with each participant first interpreting a visualization without the chatbot and then with F ACTRIA-aware chatbot guidance; no numerical effect size was reported.

D.treatment: T-NOTECHS assessed in the van Maarseveen study
D.comparison: T-NOTECHS assessed in the Steinemann study

cells.quote: The T-NOTECHS papers which used ICC were Steinemann et al [23] who had an ICC score of 0.48 for real-life resuscitations and van Maarseveen [20] et al. had an ICC of 0.94 (0.87–0.98). Steinemann et al [23] report poor reliability and van Maarseveen et al [20] report excellent reliability.
cells.note: This is a cross-study comparison of reported inter-rater reliability estimates, not a direct randomized comparison; the studies differed in context and reviewer characteristics.

cells.quote: Association between T-NOTECHS scores and ROSC did not reach statistical significance.
cells.note: Observational study of 61 emergency department thoracotomy resuscitations conducted over 24 months; no explicit comparison threshold was stated.

D.treatment: high assessment and decision-making T-NOTECHS scores
D.comparison: lower assessment and decision-making T-NOTECHS scores

cells.quote: Assessment and decision-making high scores were 5.3x more likely to lead to ROSC
cells.note: The study text reports the magnitude but does not state statistical significance or provide an interval.

cells.quote: We found an ICC of 0.94 and 0.84, respectively, when measured as the mean of three assessors or a single assessor using video analysis, while in their study an ICC of 0.48 was found for assessment of actual resuscitations by live observers.
cells.note: The study compares reliability estimates for mean ratings by three assessors with ratings by a single assessor; higher ICC indicates greater reliability.

cells.quote: When reliability was calculated for the mean of three assessors, the overall score and each domain were ‘excellent’, as the calculated ICC values were between 0.95 and 0.76. When reliability was calculated for a single assessor, the reliability was less compared to mean of three assessors.
cells.note: For three assessors, all five domains were rated excellent; for one assessor, two domains were fair and two were good.

O.outcome_detail: Cooperation and resource management domain reliability

result.effect: Average aICC 0.95 (95% CI 0.88–0.98); individual aICC 0.86 (95% CI 0.72–0.94)

cells.quote: The highest reliability was found in the domain ‘Cooperation and resource management’ (aICC = 0.95, 95% CI 0.89–0.98) and the lowest reliability was found in the domain ‘Leadership’ (aICC = 0.76. 95% 0.49–0.90) (Table 3).
cells.note: The study text reports the average and individual ICCs in Table 3; the quoted sentence identifies the three-rater average result, while the comparison value is from the same table.

result.effect: Average aICC 0.76 (95% CI 0.49–0.90); individual aICC 0.52 (95% CI 0.25–0.76)

cells.quote: The highest reliability was found in the domain ‘Cooperation and resource management’ (aICC = 0.95, 95% CI 0.89–0.98) and the lowest reliability was found in the domain ‘Leadership’ (aICC = 0.76. 95% 0.49–0.90) (Table 3).
cells.note: The study text reports the average and individual ICCs in Table 3; the quoted sentence identifies the three-rater average result, while the comparison value is from the same table.

cells.quote: When reliability was calculated for the mean of three assessors, the overall score and each domain were ‘excellent’, as the calculated ICC values were between 0.95 and 0.76. When reliability was calculated for a single assessor, the reliability was less compared to mean of three assessors. The scoring domains ‘’Leadership’ (aICC = 0.52) and ‘Situation awareness and coping with stress’ (aICC = 0.59) had a only a ‘fair’ single assessor reliability.
cells.note: This is a comparison of assessment reliability, not a learner-learning intervention.

cells.quote: When reliability was calculated for a single assessor, the reliability was less compared to mean of three assessors. The scoring domains ‘’Leadership’ (aICC = 0.52) and ‘Situation awareness and coping with stress’ (aICC = 0.59) had a only a ‘fair’ single assessor reliability.
cells.note: The three-assessor value is reported in Table 3; the text classifies single-assessor reliability as fair.

cells.quote: When reliability was calculated for a single assessor, the reliability was less compared to mean of three assessors (Table 3).
